mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last three weeks (-61.1 to -60.4 to -60.1 to -58.7), reflecting accumulating consumer confidence and habitual return to shopping; this autocorrelated momentum should persist, producing a higher 28-day mean over the next four weeks than the last.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased monotonically over the last three snapshot weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean is lower than or equal to its trailing 28-day mean despite the observed three-week upward run, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week jump in TRANSIT of more than 2 points signals renewed willingness to travel for discretionary errands; this behavioral shift translates into higher retail footfall within two weeks as commuters resume shopping trips linked to transit use.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -56.3 to -53.9 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean over the subsequent two weeks does not exceed its mean over the two weeks preceding the TRANSIT jump, the trigger mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: NYC's phased reopening of indoor dining and retail capacity continues to lift WORKPLACES mobility, which in turn sustains higher RETAIL_REC as office-adjacent commercial corridors regain foot traffic; this policy-driven co-movement should persist as long as reopening policy remains in effect.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -54.0 to -50.1 at t-0w
regime_hint: reopening phase with active indoor-dining expansion
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean fails to rise while WORKPLACES continues its upward trend, the policy-linkage hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES in the same week indicate a compounded return of commuting and work-based errands; the interaction of these two recoveries produces a larger lift in RETAIL_REC than either series moving alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increase in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rose from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's two-week forward mean rise is no larger than the rise predicted by either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES alone (i.e., no super-additive effect), the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: As the city transitions into autumn, declining outdoor comfort reduces PARKS mobility; recreation activity displaced from parks shifts toward indoor retail and dining venues, producing an inverse relationship where sustained PARKS declines are followed by RETAIL_REC increases.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -16.3 at t-1w to -20.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean does not rise following a sustained PARKS decline, the seasonal-displacement mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained persistently elevated near 14% above baseline across all four weeks, indicating an entrenched home-based lifestyle that caps discretionary retail trips; this behavioral stickiness should keep RETAIL_REC flat or declining over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 13.0 and 14.3 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's one-week forward mean rises above its trailing one-week mean while RESIDENTIAL remains flat, the behavioral-stickiness hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in GROCERY_PHARM mobility of more than 3 points suggests residents are loosening essential-only shopping discipline, a precursor behavior that spills over into general retail activity within two weeks as broader purchasing norms relax.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -28.3 to -24.4 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's two-week forward mean does not exceed its prior two-week mean following the GROCERY_PHARM jump, the spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During an active reopening regime, a concurrent decline in RESIDENTIAL alongside a rise in WORKPLACES signals compounded reduction of home-bound behavior; this joint shift interacts to drive a stronger and more durable increase in RETAIL_REC over four weeks than either series would independently predict.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls while WORKPLACES rises concurrently
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL dipped to 13.0 at t-1w then WORKPLACES rose to -50.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's four-week forward mean does not exceed its trailing four-week mean despite simultaneous RESIDENTIAL decline and WORKPLACES increase, the interaction-regime hypothesis is rejected.
